name: Sunday Times cryptic crossword, Penguin book 1 No 57

clue.text: Mark the metropolis - there’s not much of it!
Resolve to throw dice of French origin
Unsuccessful - because a bit over-organised?
Spoon, maybe, in a society centre
Royal family from Stroud
Cranky way for poets to be paid?
Pussy with a tailless style, perhaps, helps change but doesn’t change itself
A carrier of steel
Swan-song of decided taste!
Ruddy rich — too rich!
Pseudonym for Satan ?
Just the stuff for a fling after the wedding
Opening your mouth and losing your head in the shelter?
Such a justification for international government is nonsense
Go the better way to get back ?
Aversion that’s surely to Diana’s advantage
Does he count as a narrator?
Associate in training, unlikely to fall down?
Renegade from a river nation
Summoned to court and seen there, I heard
Drunken servant in appropriate surroundings
‘Shook from the tangled boughs of Heaven and Ocean, Angels of rain and —’ (Shelley: Ode to the West Wind)
Authoritative instructions for someone to take on certain engagements
Everyone needs love among conquered people
Mean to arrange a single flower
.. to produce something sweet in a trance?
Plunder with the gun
